title: For All Book Lovers: Chapter 1 (part 2)

image.attribution: User:David Monniaux, flickr user 007 Tanuki, User:Jorge Ryan, and User:ZX95 / Wikimedia Commons / CC-BY-SA-3.0

main_content:
[This article is divided into 2 parts! In part 1 we discussed other expressions that have to do with books such as: bookworm, do not judge a book by its cover, page turner, and others!]

When you do stop reading in a book you may want to think twice before dog-earring the page. To dog-ear the page of a book means to bend the top corner like a dog’s ear.

Did you know you can also read people?

To read someone like a book means you are able to understand someone very clearly. It is easy to read someone like a book when they are an open book. A person who is an open book shares their thoughts and shows their feelings very easily.

A closed book is the opposite. It describes something that is difficult to understand or a person who does not share personal details. This expression can also mean something that has ended. For example, if you have a friend who went through a divorce you could say her marriage is a closed book.

questions.question: What do you do when you bend a corner in a book?
options: You annotate the page for future reference.
You create a bookmark out of it.

questions.question: If one person understands another very well what could you say he/she can do?
options: He/she can read them like a book.
questions.answer: He/she can read them like a book.

questions.question: What is the opposite of a person who is a closed book?
options: A person who is an open book.
questions.answer: A person who is an open book.
